tests.detail: Ceftriaxone vs S. pneumoniae (meningitis): MIC=0.015 ≤ S_bp=0.5 (ratio=0.030) [EUCAST v14.0 / CLSI M100-Ed34]. Our MIC 0.015 = MIC₉₀ for penicillin-susceptible S.pn (Weinstein 2020)

Vancomycin vs S. pneumoniae (meningitis): MIC=1.0 ≤ S_bp=2.0 (ratio=0.500) [CLSI M100-Ed34]. EUCAST lists no vancomycin breakpoint for S.pneumoniae (inherently susceptible). CLSI S ≤ 1. Our value = MIC₉₀.
Rifampin vs S. pneumoniae (meningitis): MIC=0.5 = S_bp=0.5 [CLSI M100-Ed34] — AT BREAKPOINT BOUNDARY. Our MIC 0.5 within S range; used as adjunctive, not monotherapy
Linezolid vs S. pneumoniae (meningitis): MIC=2.0 = S_bp=2.0 [EUCAST v14.0 / CLSI M100-Ed34] — AT BREAKPOINT BOUNDARY. Our MIC = breakpoint boundary — susceptible but not highly so
Vancomycin vs S. aureus (MRSA): MIC=1.0 ≤ S_bp=2.0 (ratio=0.500) [EUCAST v14.0 / CLSI M100-Ed34]. MIC 1.0 = typical wild-type MRSA. MIC creep concern at 1.5-2.0.
Ceftaroline vs S. aureus (MRSA): MIC=1.0 = S_bp=1.0 [EUCAST v14.0 / CLSI M100-Ed34] — AT BREAKPOINT BOUNDARY. At breakpoint boundary — unique anti-MRSA cephalosporin via PBP2a binding
Daptomycin vs S. aureus (MRSA): MIC=0.5 ≤ S_bp=1.0 (ratio=0.500) [EUCAST v14.0 / CLSI M100-Ed34]. No EUCAST R breakpoint — 'S, dose-dependent' only. Our 0.5 = mid-range WT.
Linezolid vs S. aureus (MRSA): MIC=2.0 ≤ S_bp=4.0 (ratio=0.500) [EUCAST v14.0 / CLSI M100-Ed34]. Well within susceptible range
Clindamycin vs S. aureus (MRSA): MIC=0.25 = S_bp=0.25 [EUCAST v14.0 / CLSI M100-Ed34] — AT BREAKPOINT BOUNDARY. At EUCAST breakpoint boundary. Must test for inducible resistance (D-test).
Rifampin vs S. aureus (MRSA): MIC=0.008 ≤ S_bp=0.06 (ratio=0.133) [EUCAST v14.0 / CLSI M100-Ed34]. Highly susceptible. NEVER use as monotherapy — rapid resistance.
Isoniazid vs M. tuberculosis: MIC=0.05 ≤ S_bp=0.1 (ratio=0.500) [WHO CC (2024); CRyPTIC Consortium MIC]. Our 0.05 = wild-type MIC₅₀. Well below CC. CRyPTIC epidemiological cutoff = 0.1
Rifampin vs M. tuberculosis: MIC=0.2 ≤ S_bp=1.0 (ratio=0.200) [WHO CC (2024); CRyPTIC MIC]. Our 0.20 = well within wild-type range. CRyPTIC MIC distribution peaks at 0.125-0.25
Pyrazinamide vs M. tuberculosis (acidic): MIC=16.0 ≤ S_bp=100.0 (ratio=0.160) [WHO CC (2024)]. PZA only active at acidic pH. Our 16.0 at pH 5.5 is consistent with published MIC₅₀ 12.5-25
Ethambutol vs M. tuberculosis: MIC=2.0 ≤ S_bp=5.0 (ratio=0.400) [WHO CC (2024); CRyPTIC MIC]. Our 2.0 = within wild-type MIC range (1-5 typical)
Moxifloxacin vs M. tuberculosis: MIC=0.25 ≤ S_bp=0.5 (ratio=0.500) [WHO CC (2024); CRyPTIC MIC]. Our 0.25 = at the WHO CC boundary for low-level R. Susceptible by CLSI (S ≤ 0.5).
Bedaquiline vs M. tuberculosis: MIC=0.03 ≤ S_bp=0.25 (ratio=0.120) [WHO CC (2024, interim)]. Our 0.03 = well below CC. Published WT MIC₅₀ 0.03-0.06 (Andries 2005, Diacon 2014)
Dolutegravir vs HIV-1 (subtype B): MIC=0.51 ≤ S_bp=2.0 (ratio=0.255) [Kobayashi 2011; Stanford HIVDB v9.6]. Our 0.51 nM within published WT range. Units: nM (not μg/mL).
Tenofovir vs HIV-1 (subtype B): MIC=50.0 ≤ S_bp=100.0 (ratio=0.500) [Balzarini 1996; Ray 2016]. Our 50 nM = geometric mean of published range. Active form = TFV-diphosphate.
Emtricitabine vs HIV-1 (subtype B): MIC=8.0 ≤ S_bp=20.0 (ratio=0.400) [Schinazi 1992; Borroto-Esoda 2006]. Our 8.0 nM = within published range
Darunavir vs HIV-1 (subtype B): MIC=1.2 ≤ S_bp=5.0 (ratio=0.240) [De Meyer 2005; Stanford HIVDB v9.6]. Our 1.2 nM = within published WT range
Efavirenz vs HIV-1 (subtype B): MIC=1.0 ≤ S_bp=3.0 (ratio=0.333) [Young 1995; Stanford HIVDB v9.6]. Our 1.0 nM = geometric mean of published range

CRO + VAN (empiric bacterial meningitis) @ CSF (inflamed): Bliss=1.0000, CI=0.5438 (antagonism), clinical_eff=85%; WARNING: CI=0.54 suggests antagonism but clinical efficacy is 85%
CRO + VAN (empiric bacterial meningitis): FIC=0.013989 (synergy). Clinical efficacy 85%. Ref: Tunkel AR et al. Clin Infect Dis 2004 (IDSA Guidelines)
CRO + VAN + RIF (penicillin-R pneumococcal meningitis) @ CSF (inflamed): Bliss=1.0000, CI=0.6693 (antagonism), clinical_eff=90%; WARNING: CI=0.67 suggests antagonism but clinical efficacy is 90%
CRO + VAN + RIF (penicillin-R pneumococcal meningitis): FIC=0.034822 (synergy). Clinical efficacy 90%. Ref: van de Beek D et al. NEJM 2004; Martinez-Lacasa J et al. CID 2002
VAN + RIF (MRSA prosthetic joint) @ Bone (planktonic MIC basis): Bliss=1.0000, CI=0.9296 (antagonism), clinical_eff=82%
VAN + RIF (MRSA prosthetic joint): FIC=0.012881 (synergy). Clinical efficacy 82%. Ref: Zimmerli W et al. NEJM 2004; Lew & Waldvogel CID 2004
DAP + RIF (MRSA implant salvage) @ Bone (planktonic MIC basis): Bliss=1.0000, CI=0.9485 (antagonism), clinical_eff=78%
DAP + RIF (MRSA implant salvage): FIC=0.007048 (synergy). Clinical efficacy 78%. Ref: Byren I et al. AAC 2009; John AK et al. AAC 2009
LZD + RIF (MRSA oral step-down) @ Bone (planktonic MIC basis): Bliss=1.0000, CI=0.9492 (antagonism), clinical_eff=75%
LZD + RIF (MRSA oral step-down): FIC=0.016381 (synergy). Clinical efficacy 75%. Ref: Nguyen S et al. JAC 2009; OVIVA trial (Li HK et al. NEJM 2019)
Vancomycin: S. pneumoniae MIC=1.0 vs S. aureus (MRSA) MIC=1.0 — SAME MIC. Same WT MIC — expected (both Gram-positive cocci)
Rifampin: S. pneumoniae MIC=0.5 vs S. aureus (MRSA) MIC=0.008 — MIC₁/MIC₂ = 62.5×  (org1 less susceptible). Different MIC — EXPECTED: S. aureus natively more susceptible to RIF
Rifampin: S. pneumoniae MIC=0.5 vs M. tuberculosis MIC=0.2 — MIC₁/MIC₂ = 2.5×  (org1 less susceptible). Different MIC — EXPECTED: mycobacterial MIC differs from pneumococcal
Linezolid: S. pneumoniae MIC=2.0 vs S. aureus (MRSA) MIC=2.0 — SAME MIC. Same WT MIC — expected (both Gram-positive organisms)
Ceftriaxone: AUC=1000.0 μg·hr/mL in [600–1400] (100% of midpoint). Dose: 2g IV q12h. Ref: Patel IH Antimicrob Agents Chemother 1981; Garot D AAC 2011
Vancomycin: AUC=400.0 μg·hr/mL in [400–600] (80% of midpoint). Dose: Target AUC/MIC ≥ 400 (IDSA 2020). Ref: Rybak MJ et al. Am J Health-Syst Pharm 2020 (IDSA/ASHP/SIDP Vancomycin Guidelines)
Rifampin (meningitis): AUC=60.0 μg·hr/mL in [40–80] (100% of midpoint). Dose: 600mg IV. Ref: Nau R et al. Clin Pharmacokinet 2010
Linezolid: AUC=250.0 μg·hr/mL in [200–350] (91% of midpoint). Dose: 600mg q12h. Ref: Dryden MS JAC 2011; Brier ME AAC 2003
Dolutegravir: AUC=126400 nM·hr in [80000–180000] (97% of midpoint). Dose: 50mg daily. Ref: Song I et al. J Clin Pharmacol 2015; Min S AAC 2010
Tenofovir (TFV): AUC=7630 nM·hr in [4000–12000] (95% of midpoint). Dose: 300mg daily (prodrug TDF). Ref: Kearney BP et al. Clin Pharmacokinet 2004
Emtricitabine: AUC=40000 nM·hr in [25000–60000] (94% of midpoint). Dose: 200mg daily. Ref: Wang LH et al. Clin Pharmacol Ther 2004
Darunavir: AUC=170000 nM·hr in [120000–250000] (92% of midpoint). Dose: 800mg + 100mg RTV daily. Ref: Sekar VJ et al. AAC 2010
Efavirenz: AUC=184000 nM·hr in [130000–250000] (97% of midpoint). Dose: 600mg daily. Ref: Csajka C et al. Clin Pharmacol Ther 2003
